comparison: Perfect agreement on manual curation methodology (C62-C66). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting the empirical threshold lacks statistical justification while peer reviewers describe methods as 'robust' and 'solid' without raising this concern.

Perfect agreement on tissue consistency findings (C78-C80). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 11.6% as 'rare' is subjective, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding that 'tissue-specific escape appears relatively rare' without qualification.

Strong agreement on trisomy findings and mechanistic uncertainty (C46-C51). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval emphasizes lack of direct genetic evidence for causative variants, while peer reviewers note 'more could be done to explore genetic basis' but accept this limitation as beyond scope.

Agreement on study limitations regarding generalizability (C84-C86). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED for acknowledging limitations, while peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about 'reliance on only three individuals' and comparability across tissue types.

Strong agreement on identification of nmXCI females (C37, C43-C45). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation through UPIC rediscovery, while peer reviewers describe methods as 'solid' and 'well-documented' with no concerns.

Strong agreement on expanded scope of analysis (C3, C4, C38, C40, C59, C67). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comparison with prior work (186 vs 316 genes), while peer reviewers praise it as 'doubling the number of genes classified' and 'primary strength of this work.'

Agreement on methodological improvements (C56-C58). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides specific figure references and notes systematic comparison, while peer reviewers describe methodology as 'robust' and 'well-documented' without detailed commentary.

Divergent evaluations on frequency estimate (C5, C87). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED noting consistency with recent estimates, while peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, questioning generalizability due to 'single tissue screen' and suggesting querying all tissues for more cases.

Agreement on reclassification findings (C72-C75). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes systematic comparison with prior classifications, while peer reviewers note 'claims well-supported' and consistency across individuals as strength.

Partial overlap on variation observations (C52-C53). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN noting speculative inference without direct genetic evidence, while peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting variation as part of overall findings without challenging interpretation.

Agreement on tissue/gene coverage (C60-C61). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents coverage details clearly, while peer reviewers acknowledge breadth as strength despite single-individual limitations for some genes/tissues.

Minimal overlap on consistency findings (C68). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with specific correlation data, while peer reviewers broadly affirm consistency across individuals as adding 'weight of evidence' without specific focus on this claim.

Minimal overlap on methodological differences (C55). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting fundamental difference from prior work as important caveat, while peer reviewers incorporate consistency across individuals into broader support without specifically addressing this methodological distinction.

OpenEval evaluates biological/clinical implications (C81-C82, C6) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are logical inferences not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about disease outcomes or trait expressivity.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge and rationale (C1, C2, C23-C24, C33) as SUPPORTED, noting established knowledge appropriately applied. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.
